'If he wants it, Shaktur will have to pry my iron hauberk from my very corpse!' -Dargásh
'Shaktur? Do not speak to me of Shaktur! Speak instead of Dargásh, for only I am fit to claim the city!' -Dargásh
'In Gorthad Nûr the Dead walk. I will go there not... unless at my Prince's command.' -Beregond
'Where do you think Gwaurodel found these gloves? Ah, best not to think about it.' -Arodor
'There is no longer any rest to be found in the Deep-barrow. It is now a place of evil.' -Prince Faramir
'Do not let Khatlob sink her claws into you! If she manages it, she will throw you from the height!' -Cannoth
'Gorthad Nûr is full of bones. Tread lightly.' -Thurindol
'Disgusting. Are you really going to wear those?' -Arodor
'You leave my great-coat alone. I need it if I am to bury Shaktur!' -Dargásh
'What a vile beast! I am pleased you saw through its deception, or your bones would lie in Eithel Gwaur forever!' -Arodor
'I will not part with this tempered hauberk! It is too valuable for Orc-filth like Shaktur!' -Dargásh
'How do you think Khúrthak the Rent got that scar? Crossed Khatlob on the wrong day!' -A Gorthorog Gossip
'This coat is only to be used for special occasions, such as when I bury Shaktur in the ground!' -Dargásh
'Dargásh is weak! He will run from us, the coward!' -Shaktur
'Spirits are drawn by the stench of death. Beware armour made of bone!' -Meldir, Gossipmonger
'The wraiths tamed their fell steeds with harsh discipline and a diet of foul meats. It is a sad tale.' -Gandalf
'The winds are fierce and cold above Gath Daeroval! Only Khatlob and her brood can endure them.' -Cannoth
'The Deep-barrow was once a place of rest for the dead, but no longer. It has become wholly evil.' -Gandalf
'Like most creatures, Khatlob guards her brood with zeal. But most creatures aren't as deadly as she is!' -Cannoth
'Many of Gwaurodel's victims must lie at the bottom of the river, their remains turning to mud.' -Arodor
'Kergrim are vile carriers of disease, but the Morgul-sickness came to the Deep-barrow before them.' -Beregond
'How many fell beasts did Khatlob spawn to trouble the Free Peoples? One would be too many.' -Cannoth
'That water has not been safe to drink for many lifetimes. With the beast defeated, it may one day be pure! One day... not today.' -Arodor
'May the Ithilduin run clear once again, free of the beast that corrupted it!' -Arodor

Long have the people of Middle-earth rued the power of the Enemy to twist that which is good to its own dark ends - but now and again the truest craftsmen among the Free People find a way to redeem some of the darkest works and materials of the Enemy, and bind them to true and good purpose again. So it is with the mythical Silk-steel armours, woven from strands of silk taken from the dark brood of Shelob and her ilk, wound with threads of mithril and forged into the steel itself to craft armour of surpassing strength and lightness. Would that all such workings of the enemy could come to such elegant ends.

Long have the people of Middle-earth rued the power of the Enemy to twist that which is good to its own dark ends - but now and again the truest craftsmen among the Free People find a way to redeem some of the darkest works and materials of the Enemy, and bind them to true and good purpose again. So it is with the mythical Silk-steel armours, woven from strands of silk taken from the dark brood of Shelob and her ilk, wound with threads of mithril and forged into the steel itself to craft armour of surpassing strength and lightness. Would that all such workings of the enemy could come to such elegant ends.

Long have the people of Middle-earth rued the power of the Enemy to twist that which is good to its own dark ends - but now and again the truest craftsmen among the Free People find a way to redeem some of the darkest works and materials of the Enemy, and bind them to true and good purpose again. So it is with the mythical Silk-hide armours, woven from strands of silk taken from the dark brood of Shelob and her ilk, wound with strips of hide into the leather itself to craft armour of surpassing strength and lightness. Would that all such workings of the enemy could come to such elegant ends.

This artifact is one of the few powers that might counter the strength of the greater rings, if only for a little while.

Insect parts of all kinds can be used by the folk of Urmâkh, but whether those needs are worth the effort remains unknown to you.
The Ordâkhai warrior dropped his weapon when he was slain, putting to an end his threatening approach to Arwáth.
Babarín prepared this healing poultice to ease the hurts of the injured man recovering in Ghalbûru.
The people of Urmâkh want toad legs, but whether they are intended to be used by a cook or a healer is unknown.
The birds of Khûd Zagin are similar to others you have seen, if perhaps hardier and more aggressive.
Khôltekh gave you this parchment so you can sketch him a map to the vaults of Ashâgir.
Khôltekh gave you these orders to deliver to the warehouse keeper so she may arrange for the supplies the company will need for the journey.
The creatures who live still in Imhûlar have been stricken with a debilitating disease for which no cure has yet been found.
The reeds that grow beside the water in Ghalbûru are wide and flat, and you imagine they might be used for many different purposes.
The people of Iridír use these bristles for the creation of brushes and other small handicrafts.
The edges of these hardy leaves are sharp and might cut you if handled improperly, so you take special care.
No traveller should be without a container such as this when journeying in the arid climate of the south.
This small bronze token is marked with the crude representation of an unblinking eye. It is the symbol of the Church of the All-seeing, and that of Sauron.
This meat is lean and tough, but the Kintai must know how to prepare it in such a way that those qualities can be sufficiently overcome.
The people of Iridír make use of usan-kûni scorpion stingers for a number of purposes, both useful and decorative, but their numbers grow faster than the artisans can make use of their pieces.
You believed the jackals of Khûd Zagin were the largest and most ferocious you had ever seen, but the jackals of Urash Dâr put even those creatures to shame.
Young scholars newly in the service of Umbar are charged with picking the berries used to make the pigments and inks needed in the archives.
The people of Urmâkh have asked you to return with stingers from the scorpions that crawl throughout Imhûlar.
The satchel contained enough supplies for a journey of many days. Why would someone leave it behind?
Hármelak gave you these orders to deliver to the caravan master charged with arranging the departure of the company.
The canvas with which this pillow is fashioned is rough to the touch, but the feathers within should make for a comfortable night's rest.
The healer at Shonith gave you this cloth to dampen and then provide some relief to the sun-stricken man now in the care of the Kintai.
Written by an unknown author, this treatise on his rarely-seen and difficult to master combat style is prized by the warriors who fight on the sands of Dahâl Huliz.
The creatures who live still in Imhûlar have been stricken with a debilitating disease for which no cure has yet been found.
The Kintai performed a ritual upon these stones, and they believe their presence will protect Vartúlin from enemy incursions.
Rothog gave you these orders to deliver to the arena's famed armourer so he will know what equipment to provide for the journey.
The crebain of Urash Dâr possess terrible and frightening hooked claws of a type you have never seen before. Combined with their savage beaks, these claws can tear through flesh most rapidly.

This stone fell from Telperiën's Wall sometime during its long history, joining others of its kind on the ground. When there were enough fallen stones lying in the grass the masons abandoned efforts to replace them.
The jackals of Khûd Zagin possess teeth sharper than you have seen in other similar creatures elsewhere, but you cannot determine why that might be.

Cúridwan asked for you to retrieve these samples from the pustules of blight in Adagím. It is messy, unpleasant work, but will hopefully shed some light upon the cause of the pestilence.

Sickle-fly wings flitter so quickly as the creatures move about that the multicoloured films seem almost like rainbows. The blight in Adagím has slowed the movement of the sickle-flies to such an extent that none would mistake these unhealthy creatures for anything so beautiful.
Shoddy and ill-made as they are, it is better for travellers if these blades are stolen from the brigands watching the road through Kighân.

The dwarves of Jiret-menêsh have only recently emerged from their fastness, and they have not yet mastered the sure grip on their axes. More than a few have left their weapons behind in places of danger such as this worm-ridden height.
Given to the right person, this pass should allow Têrkar's Travellers the use of a single mûmak.

According to Irsinith, most of the spiders of Adagím are descended from a frightful creature known as Badharál the Gorger. Fortunately, the venom sacs of the spawn should be suitable enough for Irsinith's purposes and you need not seek out the creatures' legendary matriarch.
These large eggs may not serve a regiment entire, but they will go a long way toward filling the stomachs of some of Mizâdi's soldiers.
